item.title: Microsoft Launches Edge Lockdown Mode to Disable WebGL and WebGPU
item.description:
Microsoft Launches Edge Lockdown Mode to Disable WebGL and WebGPU

Microsoft has introduced a new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to reduce the browser’s attack surface.

🔍 Overview

  • Edge Lockdown Mode is inspired by Apple’s Lockdown Mode and builds on Edge Enhanced Security Mode (Super Duper Secure Mode), which disables Just‑In‑Time Compilation (JIT) in the V8 engine.
  • It blocks WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs to stop privilege‑escapable attacks.

🧩 How it Works

  • The feature focuses on the GPU process, a privileged component that handles complex graphics workloads across browser code, third‑party libraries, and device drivers.
  • When a page attempts to use WebGL or WebGPU, the address bar shows a “Lockdown Enabled” indicator.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Optional, extreme protection for users facing highly targeted attacks.
  • Designed for journalists, executives, security researchers, and administrators (Gareth Evans, Partner Security Group Manager).
  • Accepts reduced website compatibility for stronger defense.
  • Applies to devices in highly restricted environments.
  • Websites that rely on WebGL or WebGPU—especially games or maps—may not work as expected.
  • Users can test the mode in Edge Canary by:
    1. Switching to the Canary release channel.
    2. Enabling the #edge-sdsm-plus flag.
    3. Restarting the browser.
    4. Toggling on Strict mode for “Enhance your security on the web” and blocking WebGL and WebGPU graphics.
  • Microsoft estimates the feature could block around 60 % of privilege‑escalation attacks targeting Edge users.
  • Planned extensions will add more mitigations beyond the GPU process.
  • Experiment results will guide the final experience, adding clearer capability descriptions and site‑level exceptions.

🚀 Availability

  • Currently available only in the Edge Canary channel.
  • Requires a browser restart after enabling the flag.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Provides high‑risk users with an extra layer of defense against targeted cyberattacks.
  • Reduces the attack surface by preventing GPU‑based sandbox escapes.
  • Complements Microsoft’s other security enhancements such as the Edge scareware sensor and the recent restrictions on Internet Explorer mode.

#Edge #LockdownMode #Cybersecurity #BrowserSecurity #WebGL

Source: Microsoft tests new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables GPU APIs

item.title: Microsoft releases Windows 11 KB5132057 November optional cumulative update
item.description:
Microsoft releases Windows 11 KB5132057 November optional cumulative update

Microsoft released the KB5132057 November optional cumulative update for Windows 11 versions 25H2 and 26H2, bringing 28 changes including improvements to Windows Search, Windows Hello, and the Run dialog. This preview update allows IT administrators to test improvements, bug fixes, and new features before the next Patch Tuesday release, and it will be the final non-security preview update released this year as operations wind down for the Western holidays.

🔍 Overview

KB5132057 is an optional non-security preview update that provides only quality improvements rather than security fixes. Installing this update will upgrade Windows 11 26H2 and 25H2 devices to builds 26300.10075 and 26200.10075, respectively. Microsoft also noted that a limited number of consumer and business devices might experience one additional restart during installation after a Secure Boot certificate update is applied.

⚙️ Key features and changes

  • Windows Search: Features a new WinUI 3-based Search Box experience that removes promotional content from web results for better resource efficiency and streamlined design. Search from This PC in File Explorer is now indexer-based, and inline actions let users complete common tasks directly from Windows Search.
  • Windows Hello: Includes improved facial recognition enabling sign-in in dark rooms after turning on the “Automatically adjust screen brightness during face recognition” setting.
  • Run Dialog: Adds the new Run dialog with a refreshed design and an almost instant time-to-show of 94 ms.
  • Accessibility: Users can now turn off accidentally triggered keyboard shortcuts for Sticky Keys, Filter Keys, or Toggle Keys directly from the appearing prompt.
  • Enterprise and Security: Web sign-in is now supported on Microsoft Entra hybrid-joined devices, allowing password-free lock screen sign-in via FIDO2 keys, phone passkeys, or Temporary Access Pass.
  • Bug Fixes: Resolves an issue where the File History restore interface might not find backups when a drive is selected as the backup location.
Feature / Component Description
Windows Search Box Built on WinUI 3, removes promotional web content for streamlined design.
Inline Actions Complete tasks like turning on dark mode/Bluetooth, adjusting brightness, or managing open windows directly from search.
Phone Link Integration Call or text contacts, and use “Find my phone” and “Do Not Disturb” actions if an Android phone is connected.
Windows Hello Improved facial recognition for signing into accounts in dark rooms.

🚀 Availability

  • Users can install the update by opening Windows Settings, clicking Windows Update, and clicking ‘Check for Updates’.
  • Because it is an optional update, users must click the “Download and install” link unless they have the “Get the latest updates as soon as they’re available” option enabled.
  • The preview update can also be manually downloaded and installed from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

#Windows11 #Microsoft #WindowsUpdate #TechNews

Source: Windows 11 KB5132057 update released with 28 changes and fixes
